pr_body:
This patch reworks how Incompatible Target Skipping is implemented.

The biggest change is that incompatibility is now checked earlier. This
allows us to avoid evaluating dependencies (such as toolchains) in
situations where a target is "directly" incompatible. "Direct incompatibility"
refers to incompatibility due to a target's `target_compatible_with` value.

Moving the incompatibility checking earlier had the undesired effect of
visibility restrictions being ignored on incompatible targets. This is
tracked in #16044. As per
https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/14096#issuecomment-1189589626,
we will fix it in a separate patch.

Fixes #12897.

I think the question becomes: If target A depends on an incompatible target B whose visibility restriction excludes A, what do you want to happen?
The current PR here makes it so that A becomes incompatible without any visibility errors.
If we want visibility errors to be thrown, then I'll have to do some serious thinking. It would be nice if we could call into `CommonPrerequisiteValidator`, but as-is that's not an option.

To clarify: I think the behaviour of the code in this PR here is incorrect. Visibility errors _should_ take priority over incompatibility propagation. What do you think about this?

I'm just not sure yet how to reconcile that priority with how late in the analysis phase visibility is checked.
Can we move visibility checking earlier? I haven't reviewed that code recently, @gregestren may have some ideas.

I agree with you that principally visibility checking should happen first - that's the right user experience.

That said, I think it's going to be hard to refactor visibility. Visibility's implementation has a lot of subtle dependencies and I don't think it's easy to, like, just move some `checkVisibility()` function from class A to class B. I say this from experience. :p 

If you see a reasonable way forward on that, let's push on it. If it looks like it's a serious blocker to this feature, I could be convinced for us to replace that with a `TODO: get visibility / incompatible error precedence right`, in the name of getting a nice user experience improvement today at the cost of a somewhat obscure error scenario.
